/.difference: '/' is the top of the full filesystem tree, while /root is root user's home directory.

/bin.difference: /bin has essential user commands, /sbin is mostly for system administration.

/etc.difference: /etc stores local machine configuration; /usr stores package-provided programs and data.

/home.difference: /home is for normal users, /root is specifically for the root account.

/lib.difference: /lib historically contains essential libs needed early in boot; /usr/lib holds broader userland libs.

/tmp.difference: /tmp is often cleared at reboot; /var/tmp is expected to survive longer.

/var.difference: /var contains changing but persistent data, while /tmp is short-lived scratch space.
